# Draft:Professor Oluwole Familoni Award for the Best Graduating Student in Organic Chemistry

----
The Professor Oluwole Familoni Award for the Best Graduating Student in Organic Chemistry is a prestigious academic honor conferred by the University of Lagos, Nigeria. Established in recognition of the contributions of Oluwole Babafemi Familoni, a distinguished chemist and professor, the award is presented annually to the top-performing student in organic chemistry.
Background
The award is named after Oluwole Babafemi Familoni, a renowned Nigerian organic chemist and academic administrator. Born on November 24, 1957, he earned his B.Sc. in Chemistry (Second Class Upper Division) in 1981, M.Phil. in Chemistry in 1986, and Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry in 1990, all from the University of Lagos. Over the years, he has held several key positions, including:
* Sub-Dean of the Faculty of Science (2000–2002)
* Head of the Department of Chemistry (2002–2005)
* Dean of the Faculty of Science (2008–2012)
* Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic and Research) at the University of Lagos
His research focuses on the synthesis of heterocyclic compounds, natural product chemistry, and physiologically active molecules. Professor Familoni is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry, London and a multiple-time recipient of the JWT Jones Travelling Fellowship from the same institution.
Criteria for the Award
The Professor Oluwole Familoni Award for the Best Graduating Student in Organic Chemistry is a prestigious recognition granted to the most outstanding student in organic chemistry at the University of Lagos. The recipient is selected based on the following criteria:
1. Academic Excellence: The candidate must achieve the highest cumulative points across all major organic chemistry courses, demonstrating superior mastery of the subject matter. Key courses considered include:
* Natural Product Chemistry – Understanding the chemistry of naturally occurring compounds and their applications.
* Methods of Organic Synthesis – Mastery of synthetic strategies, reaction mechanisms, and modern synthetic methodologies.
* Bioactive Organic Chemistry – Exploration of bioactive molecules and their roles in pharmaceutical and medicinal chemistry.
2. Conceptual and Practical Proficiency: Candidates must exhibit a deep understanding of organic chemistry principles, with a strong grasp of both theoretical concepts and their practical applications in laboratory settings.
3. Research and Innovation: The award prioritizes students who have demonstrated strong research potential, particularly in organic synthesis, natural product chemistry, or related areas. Contributions to published research, final-year projects, or innovative approaches to organic synthesis are highly regarded.
4. Ethical and Professional Standards: The recipient must uphold the highest standards of integrity, professionalism, and academic discipline, serving as a role model for peers within the department.
The selection process is rigorous, with faculty members from the Department of Chemistry evaluating candidates based on academic records, research contributions, and overall impact on the scientific community. The award aims to inspire and encourage students to pursue excellence in organic chemistry, fostering innovation and advancements in the field.
Selection Process
The selection committee, consisting of senior faculty members from the Department of Chemistry at the University of Lagos, evaluates students based on:
* Academic transcripts and overall performance in organic chemistry courses.
* Research projects and laboratory work.
* Recommendations from faculty members.
Notable Recipients
One of the distinguished recipients of this award is Mubarak Ayinla, who graduated with First-Class Honours in Chemistry (Pure and Applied) from the University of Lagos in 2017. He later pursued a Ph.D. in Chemistry at the University of Massachusetts Lowell, focusing on Organic Synthesis, Dynamic Covalent Chemistry, and Materials Science. Mubarak Ayinla has also received the Scholars Endowment from the University of Lagos.
Another notable recipient is Olamilekan Julius, who was honored with the award in 2023 for achieving a perfect GPA in major organic chemistry courses. His exceptional academic performance and research contributions in synthetic organic chemistry earned him widespread recognition. Julius is actively engaged in cutting-edge research and continues to make strides in the field of organic synthesis.
Impact
The award serves as a motivation for students to excel in organic chemistry, fostering a culture of academic excellence and research innovation at the University of Lagos. It also strengthens the legacy of Professor Familoni by inspiring future generations of chemists.
